title: Living Independently L1 · Where Does Money Come From?
tag: ASDAN LIVING INDEPENDENTLY · Module 1 · Lesson 1 · BUILD · Slot 3 (Version A)
sub: Money in · Money out · My money map
learningObjective: To sort money coming in from money going out.
successCriteria: I can name three ways money comes IN.
I can name three ways money goes OUT.
I can make my own money map with real examples.
scText: By the end you will have handled and counted a real wage packet, sorted income from spending, and built your money map — your first evidence for ASDAN Living Independently Module 1 (Section A).
aspire1: use the words income and spending out loud.
aspire2: find the item whose price surprised you most and say why.

arrival.heading: Money IN or money OUT?
arrival.tipWait: tell your partner the last thing you spent money on — anything counts.

starter.heading: If money appeared in your pocket right now… where did it come from?
starter.prompt: With your partner: list every way a person can GET money. Real ways — jobs, gifts, benefits, selling things, finding it down the sofa. All of it.
starter.stems:
“One way to get money is…”
“Adults I know get money from…”
“When I am older my money will come from…”
starter.hint: Think about the adults in your life: how does money arrive for them? Weekly? Monthly? In cash or into a bank?

iDo.heading: Money IN and money OUT
cards: Money you EARN from a job. Usually paid into a bank every week or month.
Money from the government to help people who need it — that is what it is for.
Birthday money, pocket money, money from selling your old stuff.
Money OUT: food, bus fare, phone, games, clothes. Out is easier than in!
iDo.miscWrong: “Money comes from the cash machine / from your phone.”
iDo.miscRight: The machine only hands over money that already came IN — from wages, benefits or gifts. No income in, nothing comes out.

weDo.heading: Sort it: money IN or money OUT?
weDo.hint: Ask: does this put money INTO your pocket, or take it OUT?

practical.heading: Money stations 💷
practical.tip: real money stays on the table mats. We count it, we respect it, it all goes back in the tin. That is exactly how tills work in real jobs.
stations: A real (practice) wage packet of coins and notes. Count it with a partner and record the total. Check: does it match the payslip amount? That checking skill is Module 2 next half term.
Real items with real price tags around the room. Find them, record the prices, and rank them cheapest to dearest. Verdict: which one is worth its price?
Big paper, you in the middle. Arrows IN (where your money comes from now, and where it will come from at 18). Arrows OUT (where it goes). Honest maps only.

overlay: Module 1 evidence banked — your first steps toward the Living Independently certificate.
taBriefs: Meet & greet. Money tins counted BEFORE the lesson; mats on tables.
Arrival task: no adult answers. Money can be a sensitive home topic — keep it matter-of-fact and judgement-free all lesson.
LO slide: read together. Pre-teach 'income' — money IN.
Starter: accept benefits as a completely normal answer, stated plainly. Scribe all suggestions.
I Do: pupils listening. The benefits card is deliberately neutral and dignified — keep it that way.
We Do: rotate tapping. 'Selling old games' trips people — good discussion moment.
PRACTICAL: you run Count the Wage Packet — support 1:1 counting, model the recount habit. Money back in tin, count it again at the end.
Evidence: photograph maps + counted packets. Scribe sentences where needed, note 'TA scribed'. No pupil's personal family finances are recorded — maps use general sources.
Exit ticket: alone, one tap. Recount the money tin with a pupil helper.
